en.name: Coriander, fresh
en.summary: Fresh coriander keeps 1–2 weeks at room temperature with its stems in water, or 2–3 weeks in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. It is a soft-stemmed, thin-leafed herb, so it fails fast once it gets wet or bruised.
en.pantry: 1–2 weeks with the stems trimmed and standing in a couple of centimetres of water, away from direct sun, and change the water daily. Treating a bunch like a bouquet is genuinely the best you can do at room temperature: coriander draws water up the stem and stays perky, while a bunch lying on the worktop wilts within a day. Do not cover the leaves tightly — they need air, and trapped humidity around the leaf is what turns a bunch black.
en.fridge: 2–3 weeks at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, which is where a bunch will keep longest. Two methods work: stems in a jar of water with a loose bag over the top, or the whole bunch wrapped in dry kitchen paper inside a box. Either way, do not wash it until you use it, and go through the bunch every few days pulling out blackened leaves. Coriander bruises where it is squashed, so store it somewhere it will not be crushed by a bag of vegetables.
en.freezer: Freeze damage will appear, so no freezer timeline is given. The leaves go dark and limp because they are thin and full of water. They are still useful for cooking, though: chop the leaves and stems, pack them into an ice-cube tray with a little water or oil, and drop a cube into a curry or a soup. The stems, which carry as much flavour as the leaves, are the part most worth saving this way.
en.thawing: Add frozen coriander cubes straight to a hot pan or a simmering dish. Do not thaw them first, and do not expect to garnish with thawed leaves.
spoilage: Blackened, translucent leaves that have gone slimy.
A sour or fermented smell instead of the herb's sharp, citrusy one.
Slime at the cut ends or cloudy water in the jar.
Yellow, papery leaves from a bunch that dried out.
tips: Stand the bunch in water and change it daily; it works at room temperature and in the fridge.
Do not wash until you use it — wet leaves collapse.
Use the stems; they carry as much flavour as the leaves and keep better.
Freeze chopped stems and leaves in oil cubes for cooking.

faq.q: How long does fresh coriander keep?
faq.a: 1–2 weeks at room temperature with the stems in water, or 2–3 weeks in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
Freeze damage will appear, so no timeline is given. Chopped and frozen in oil or water cubes it is excellent for cooking, but not for garnish.

faq.q: How do you stop coriander going black in the fridge?
faq.a: Keep the leaves dry and give them air. Stems in water with a loose bag, or a dry paper wrap in an open box, and never washed until use.

zh.name: 香菜
zh.summary: 新鮮香菜把莖插在水裡放常溫可放 1～2 週，放 4 °C 以下冷藏則是 2～3 週。它是莖軟葉薄的香草，一旦碰到水或被壓到，就壞得很快。
zh.pantry: 把莖剪一下、插進約兩公分深的水裡，放在不直曬的地方，每天換水，1～2 週。在常溫下，把一把香菜當成一束花來照顧，真的就是最好的辦法：香菜會從莖把水吸上去、維持挺立，而平放在檯面上的那一把，一天就軟掉了。葉子不要包緊——它們需要空氣，而困在葉片周圍的濕氣正是把一整把香菜變黑的原因。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下 2～3 週，這是一把香菜能撐最久的地方。兩種方法都有效：莖插進水杯、上面鬆鬆罩一個袋子；或整把用乾的廚房紙巾包好放進盒子。無論哪一種，都要到使用時才洗，並且每隔幾天翻一下，把變黑的葉子挑掉。香菜被壓到就會出現瘀傷，所以請放在不會被一袋蔬菜壓住的位置。
zh.freezer: 冷凍會出現凍傷，所以沒有給期限。葉子又薄又滿是水，凍過會變深、變軟塌。但它拿來煮還是很好用：把葉子和莖切碎，填進製冰盒、加一點水或油，要用時丟一塊進咖哩或湯裡。最值得用這個方法留下來的是莖——它的香氣不輸葉子。
zh.thawing: 香菜冰塊直接丟進熱鍋或滾著的菜裡，不要先解凍，也不要期待解凍後的葉子還能擺盤。
spoilage: 葉子發黑、變透明、摸起來黏滑。
聞起來酸或有發酵味，而不是那股銳利帶柑橘感的香氣。
切口變黏滑，或杯子裡的水變混濁。
葉子發黃、乾成紙片，那是整把乾掉了。
tips: 整把插水、每天換水；常溫和冷藏都適用。
要用時才洗——濕掉的葉子會塌。
莖不要丟，它的香氣不輸葉子，而且更耐放。
把切碎的莖和葉用油做成冰塊冷凍，料理時很好用。

faq.a: 莖插水放常溫 1～2 週，或 4 °C 以下冷藏 2～3 週。
冷凍會凍傷，所以沒有給期限。切碎後用油或水做成冰塊冷凍，拿來煮非常好用，但不能擺盤。

faq.q: 香菜放冰箱怎麼避免變黑？
faq.a: 讓葉子保持乾燥並且有空氣。莖插水、上面鬆罩袋子，或用乾紙巾包好放敞口盒，而且要用時才洗。

faq.q: 市場買的一大把香菜，放冰箱三天就黑掉了，是怎麼回事？
faq.a: 多半是水和壓傷。香菜葉很薄，攤販裝袋前又常噴水，那些水困在葉片之間散不掉，就從那裡開始發黑變黏；上面再壓一袋菜，瘀傷處更是提早投降。回家請先整把攤開，把黑掉和爛掉的挑出來，然後挑一種做法：莖剪一下插進一點水裡、上面鬆鬆罩個袋子，或整把用乾的廚房紙巾包好放進敞口盒——兩種的重點都是葉子要乾、要有空氣。放 4 °C 以下、要用時才洗，可以撐到 2～3 週；千萬不要為了省事先把整把洗好再冰。
